caption:
Synthesia turns a prompt, a document or a script into a video read by an AI avatar.
The free plan gives you 10 minutes of video a month, with a watermark and no downloads.
The full step by step guide, with scripts to copy and the plan limits, is on neurafeedai.com.

threads_text: Synthesia makes a video with an AI presenter from a prompt, a PDF or a script, and the free plan covers 10 minutes a month with a watermark. One reviewer still says some viewers find the avatars a little unsettling. Would you sit through a training video read by an AI avatar?

slides.headline: How to use *Synthesia* to make AI avatar videos

slides.heading: 1. Start with a *prompt*
paras: Describe the topic, the audience and the goal, or attach a PDF, slides or a Word file.
Pick a length: Auto, Short, Medium or Long.

slides.heading: 2. Check the *outline*
paras: Synthesia drafts the scenes and the script first.
Edit, delete or add sections before you build the video.

slides.heading: 3. Pick an *avatar* and voice
paras: The editor works like slides: scenes on the left, the script at the bottom.
Choose the avatar and voice, then add text, media or captions.

slides.heading: 4. Generate and *share*
paras: Click Generate, then share a link, embed it or download an MP4.
The free plan has a watermark and no downloads.

site_article.headline: How to use Synthesia, and is it worth it: steps, scripts and plan limits

site_article.hero_alt: Synthesia's title image for its guide on how to create videos with the platform.

paragraphs.text: Here is how to use Synthesia in one line: give it a prompt, a file or a script, check the outline it drafts, pick an avatar and a voice, and click Generate. Synthesia is an AI video platform that makes videos with AI presenters, motion graphics and B-roll, without a camera. The company says no experience is needed, compares its editor to PowerPoint, and says videos can be made in more than 140 languages.

It is built for work videos more than social clips. Synthesia lists training, onboarding, product demos, internal updates, sales enablement and marketing explainers as the usual uses. You can also add quizzes, clickable hotspots and branching scenes for training.
How to use Synthesia: your first video

paragraphs.title: 1. Start a video from a prompt
paragraphs.text: According to the Help Center, you click Video on the Home screen, choose Studio in the creation mode menu and describe the topic, the audience and the goal in the prompt box. You can attach PDFs, PowerPoint files, Word documents or URLs, and pick a length: Auto, Short, Medium or Long. This Assistant flow is listed for the Starter, Pro, Team and Enterprise plans, and Synthesia says it does not use credits.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: A short training video from a description
paragraphs.text:
Topic: how to report a phishing email at work.
Audience: office staff with no security background.
Goal: after the video, viewers know the three signs of a phishing email and exactly who to report it to.
Tone: friendly and plain. Keep it under 2 minutes and end with one clear action.

paragraphs.title: 2. Choose a style
paragraphs.text: Before the video is built you set a delivery style, Presentation or Dynamic, where Dynamic adds B-roll. You can leave the template on Auto or pick one. Brand kits need the Team or Enterprise plan, so on other plans choose No Brand Kit.

paragraphs.title: 3. Fix the outline before you generate
paragraphs.text: Synthesia shows a numbered outline of sections. Edit the text, delete a section or add one, then choose Generate video, or Continue to editor if you want to check every scene first. This is the cheapest moment to change your mind.

paragraphs.title: 4. Or paste your own script
paragraphs.text: If you already know what the avatar should say, use Import script from the Home screen instead. Each paragraph separated by a blank line becomes its own scene, and the Help Center says the Assistant uses your script as written, without rewriting it.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: A three scene script to import
paragraphs.text:
Hi, I'm [name], and in the next minute you'll learn how to book time off in [tool].

Open [tool], go to your profile, and choose the dates you want off. Add a short note for your manager.

That's it. Your manager gets a message and you'll see the answer within [number] days. Questions? Ask [team or channel].
Edit, refine and share

paragraphs.title: 5. Refine it in the Storyboard
paragraphs.text: After creation you land in the Storyboard, with the script, the visuals and an Assistant chat side by side. Ask the chat to shorten the video, change the tone or rewrite a scene, or use the quick actions on a scene: Improve writing, Shorten, Longer and Change tone. Collapse takes you back to the canvas for scene by scene editing.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: A refinement request for the Assistant chat
paragraphs.text: Make the whole video about 30 percent shorter. Keep the hook in the first scene and the call to action in the last scene. Replace any jargon with plain words and keep the tone friendly.

paragraphs.title: 6. Pick the avatar, voice and visuals
paragraphs.text: In the editor, scenes sit on the left and the script box for narration sits at the bottom. The toolbar holds the avatar, text, shapes, media, captions, quizzes and a screen recorder. Choose an avatar and a voice that fit your audience, then add B-roll from the stock library, your own footage or AI generation.

Synthesia's own advice is one clear idea per scene, a hook in the first 5 seconds and a clear call to action near the end. Read the script out loud before you generate: the avatar will say exactly what you typed.

paragraphs.title: 7. Generate and share
paragraphs.text: Click Generate. Synthesia suggests a quick check first: play the preview, look at pacing and transitions, and turn on captions. When it is done you can download an MP4, share a link, embed it on a page or export a SCORM package for a learning system.
Synthesia plans and limits

The free Basic plan includes 10 minutes of Studio video a month, 9 AI avatars and 500 credits. Videos carry a Synthesia watermark, and downloads and logo removal are not included, so you share by link only.

Starter costs $19 a month, or $14 a month billed yearly at $168, and adds downloads, logo removal, more than 125 avatars and 3 personal avatars. Pro costs $89 a month, or $59 a month billed yearly at $708, with up to about 60 minutes of Studio video a month and more than 180 avatars. Team is for 1 to 5 members sharing one credit pool and adds brand kits and SCORM export; Enterprise, for 6 or more members, adds unlimited Studio video and SSO.

Synthesia's pricing page showed a Black Friday offer for new customers in late November 2026, and plan names have changed before: the older Personal plan is now in maintenance mode. Check the pricing page on the day you buy.
When Synthesia is worth it

Wyzowl, a video production company, rated Synthesia 4.5 out of 5 and praised its speed and cost compared with filming. It also listed the weak spots: an avatar cannot fully replace the human touch of a real presenter, some viewers may find the avatars a little unsettling, and you cannot see the avatar move until the video is rendered, which slows down editing.

Synthesia makes the most sense when you need many clear, similar videos: training, onboarding, how to videos for staff, or the same message in several languages. It is a weaker fit for content where a real face and personality carry the message. Use the free 10 minutes to make one real video for your actual audience and show it to a few people. If nobody minds the avatar, the paid plans are easy to judge against the cost of filming.
